findings.title: Per-client permission lookup uses client.getId() as resource name, but resources are keyed by client ID resolved through resolveClient
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the per-client resource is looked up with resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()). However, AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (AdminPermissionsSchema.java lines 93-95 and 175-184) creates client resources with the name set to resolveClient(session, id), which returns client.getId() — the internal ID. This is consistent only if the permission was created with the internal client ID. But the test PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient creates the permission with myclient.getId() (the internal ID from the admin client representation), so it works there. The real problem: when a permission is created via the REST API using the clientId (e.g. 'myclient') rather than the internal UUID, getOrCreateResource resolves it to the internal ID and creates the resource named by the internal ID — consistent. However, if a resource already exists under a different name (e.g. created by an older flow or by name), findByName with client.getId() will miss it and silently fall through to the all-clients resource, potentially granting broader permissions than intended or denying narrower ones. More critically, the fallback logic at lines 217-221 calls getResourceTypeResource and then findByResource(server, resource) — if resource is null (no 'Clients' type resource exists), findByResource will NPE or misbehave. Also, the evaluation uses resource.getScopes() which for a per-client resource includes ALL scopes of the Clients type (set in getOrCreateResource line 106), meaning a permission granting only 'view' on a specific client will still evaluate against all scopes — but the code then filters by expectedScopes, so this is OK. The core issue is the fragile name-based lookup mixing internal IDs and the null-resource dereference risk at line 219 when getResourceTypeResource returns null.
